description:
I am an AI engineer focused on agentic workflows, RAG systems, and AI safety. For NASA Space Apps, I am developing Flame in Freefall, an AI-powered research assistant that analyzes NASA's microgravity combustion data.

Built with Python, LangGraph, and Groq, it retrieves verified experiment information, including FLEX and BASS, and applies governance guardrails to prevent unsupported outputs. When evidence or confidence is insufficient, it refuses to provide unverified safety insights.
summary:
"Flame in Freefall" is an interactive, AI-governed web dashboard designed to synthesize, rank, and interpret decades of NASA microgravity combustion research from the Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database.

What we developed: A Streamlit-based application powered by the Groq API that indexes verified NASA investigation records (including PSI-10, SAFFIRE, and ACME data) and provides an intuitive Mission Control interface for complex queries.

How it addresses the challenge: It transforms dense, fragmented physical science data into immediate, searchable insights regarding flame behavior, droplet combustion, and flammability limits. It integrates strict AI governance guardrails to cross-verify outputs against grounded experimental records and automatically refuse out-of-scope prompts, ensuring zero hallucinations.

Why it is important: As human spaceflight shifts toward sustained Artemis Moon bases and future Mars missions, habitats will utilize higher oxygen concentrations (~30%+) and lower pressures, drastically escalating fire risks. Flame in Freefall empowers aerospace engineers and safety researchers with rapid, reliable data access to optimize material selection, spacecraft design, and fire suppression systems for safer space exploration.
details:
Flame in Freefall is an interactive, AI-governed dashboard designed to synthesize, rank, and interpret NASA’s microgravity combustion data from the Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database. Organized into a sleek Mission Control interface, the platform features three core modules: an Overview & Ranking view to compare investigations using transparent safety heuristics, a Moon/Mars Insights module highlighting flammability risks in altered atmospheres, and an interactive Agent Hub that answers complex scientific queries using grounded NASA experimental records (such as PSI-10, PSI-84, SAFFIRE, and ACME).

Benefits & Intended Impact Decades of microgravity combustion research are dense and difficult for engineers to rapidly cross-reference. Flame in Freefall turns fragmented scientific records into immediate, actionable fire safety intelligence. As NASA prepares for sustained Artemis lunar habitats and Mars missions—where elevated oxygen concentrations (30%+) and reduced pressures drastically increase material flammability—this tool accelerates safer material selection, fire detection, and suppression planning. Additionally, these microgravity insights support terrestrial fire safety advancements, such as fine-water-mist extinguishers and improved protective gear.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Language: Python
  • Frontend & UI: Streamlit (custom space-grade dashboard styling)
  • AI & Reasoning Engine: Groq API (openai/gpt-oss-120b)
  • Data & Environment: JSON structured experimental schemas, python-dotenv for secure credential handling, and Git/GitHub for version control.

Creativity & Key Design Factors Rather than building a generic chatbot prone to fabricating scientific data, we engineered a governance-first architecture. Every AI response is strictly bounded to verified NASA PSI parameters and DOI citations, featuring an automated refusal mechanism that blocks out-of-scope or unsupported queries to guarantee zero hallucinations. We also prioritized lightweight, modular execution so aerospace researchers, educators, and students can deploy and query critical fire safety data effortlessly.
